properties.rationale:
ACCEPTED AS ARCHITECTURE, NOT REPAIRED. Every path between subsystems routes through the MCP protocol because that is what reflow2 IS: an agent-native design brain whose entire surface is served over MCP. The detector is correct that the topology has one articulation point; it is wrong only in the implied remedy, `add_redundancy`, which would mean a second protocol nobody wants and no consumer asked for.

⚠️ THE COST OF LEAVING IT OPEN IS THE REASON THIS IS ACKNOWLEDGED RATHER THAN IGNORED. Three permanent warnings in one category teach a reader to skim it, and the next single point of failure — a real one, in a place nobody chose — would arrive into a list already being skipped. This project has found that wallpaper failure three times (unreviewed_ideas at 111 of 186, the undeclared-seam list, the unallocated-parts list). Moving it into `reviewed_defects` keeps it visible and counted while restoring the open list's ability to mean something.

📌 THE REVIEW EXPIRES IF THE SHAPE CHANGES, which is the property that makes this safe: the defect id hashes the category with the affected set, so if this interface stops being the sole bridge — or a different one becomes one — the new shape has a new id nobody has accepted, and it surfaces again.

⚠️ NOT ACCEPTED: that a single point of failure here is harmless. `rule:mcp-and-the-graph-are-the-only-common-ground` makes this seam load-bearing on purpose, and its availability is a real operational property. What is accepted is that the DESIGN is right and the detector's suggested repair is not.
